title: A machine for checking the canonical front
statement: For every machine format $F$, there exist a finite Boolean-alphabet Turing machine $C$, an entry state, an injective assignment of exit states to the three values in $\{\mathrm{none},\mathrm{some\ false},\mathrm{some\ true}\}$, and a natural number $a$, with at least four work tapes, such that the following holds for every Boolean input $x$. At some time $t\le a(|x|+1)$, starting with all work tapes blank, the machine is in the assigned exit state for a verdict, has produced no output, and has not previously visited any exit state. If the verdict is not $\mathrm{some\ true}$, then decoding $x$ returns the fallback code. If the verdict is $\mathrm{some\ true}$, then $x$ parses as $bits$ and $rest$, the binary representation of the value of $bits$ is exactly $bits$, and $\max\{guard,(4k+5)3^{k+1}\}(v+1)\le |rest|$, where $k$ is the work-tape count of $F$ and $v$ is the binary value of $bits$. At that time the input-head position is $2|bits|+3$; every work tape other than tape $1$ is at position zero and contains the canonical count word for $bits$ on tape $0$, the canonical offset word for $bits$ on tape $2$, and the empty word on all remaining tapes.
hypotheses_covered: The constructed machine has at least four work tapes
For each Boolean input, a bounded time and a verdict exist
The machine reaches the verdict’s exit state and has empty output
No exit state was visited earlier
If the verdict is not true, decoding returns the fallback code
If the verdict is true, the input has a canonical parsed header and sufficient guard length
If the verdict is true, the specified input-head position and work-tape contents and positions hold
